logline: A razor-sharp advertising executive fights her way to become the first female CEO of a top Korean agency - a workplace drama about ambition, betrayal, and the cost of power.

renewal.note: Completed 16-episode run on JTBC from January 7 to February 26, 2023. Final episode recorded a 16.044% nationwide rating, placing it among the top 5 highest-rated JTBC dramas of all time.

bollymeter.basis: Lee Bo-young's performance as the calculating and driven Go Ah-in is the season's load-bearing element. Commercial reception was exceptional - a 16.044% finale rating made it one of the top-rated JTBC dramas in network history, averaging 9.95% nationwide.

seasons.review_body: Agency arrived in January 2023 riding the prestige slot JTBC cleared after Reborn Rich, and it rewarded that inheritance with numbers: the series averaged 9.95% nationwide and its finale hit 16.044%, placing it in the top 5 highest-rated dramas in JTBC history. The premise is elemental - Go Ah-in, raised in poverty, claws her way toward becoming the first female executive of a major advertising conglomerate. Lee Bo-young's performance as the calculating and driven executive anchors every scene. IMDb audience ratings settled at 7.8, reflecting warm but not rapturous consensus - the show's emphasis on office politics over emotional warmth divided viewers who wanted more personal drama alongside the corporate ladder-climbing. The writing is precise and the stakes feel genuinely adult in ways much K-drama avoids. A workplace drama that earns its ambition.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere wastes no time establishing Go Ah-in as someone who calculates every room before entering it. Lee Bo-young commands the screen from the first scene, and the advertising world backdrop feels researched rather than decorative.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Go Ah-in's first boardroom play - an opening move that signals exactly what kind of show this will be.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers on the show's core promise without sentimentalising its protagonist. Whether Go Ah-in deserves the ending she gets is precisely the question the final hour forces the audience to sit with.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The boardroom resolution that had Korean audiences driving the show to a 16% nationwide rating peak.
